chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Whichever man falls upon a slave girl of a people unlawfully, then buys her, then claims her child, so he would not inherit from him anything.
For the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The child is for the bed, and for the adulterer is the stone.
And the son of the adultery would not inherit except a man who claims a son of his slave girl.
And whichever man accepts his child, then denies from it, so that is not for him.
Nor is it honourable; his child would be attached to him whether it was from his wife or from his slave girl.

key_terms.الْوَلَدُ لِلْفِرَاشِ: The child is for the bed (place of lawful intercourse)

ai.seo_question: What is the inheritance status of a child born to a slave girl from unlawful intercourse if the man buys her and claims the child?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the inheritance status of a child born to a slave girl after her owner commits unlawful intercourse with her, ruling that he does not inherit from her child despite his claim. It reinforces the Prophetic maxim 'the child is for the bed' (al-waladu lil-firash), emphasizing that legitimate lineage is tied to the marital union, while the adulterer receives his 'due' (the stone). Furthermore, it establishes that a man cannot disown a child he has acknowledged if the mother is his wife or slave girl, ensuring the child's rights remain intact.
